editorial.body: (사설) 전국 교정 시설 과밀 수용률이 126%에 이르러 교정 공무원의 업무 환경 악화, 정신질환·마약사범 증가 등 문제가 심화되고 있습니다. 인권 침해와 교화 효과 저하 우려로 시급한 개선책이 필요합니다. |
summary: 전국 교정시설 과밀 수용률이 126%까지 치솟았다.

인권 침해와 교화 효과 저하를 막기 위해 즉각적인 개선이 시급하다.

editorial.titleTr: Overcrowded Prison Cells Push South Korea's Correctional Facilities to the Brink
summaryTr: Overcrowding rates at correctional facilities nationwide have surged to 126%.
A vicious cycle is repeating due to deteriorating work conditions for correctional officers and rising numbers of inmates with mental illness and drug offenses.
Immediate improvements are urgently needed to prevent human rights violations and declining rehabilitation effectiveness.
editorial.bodyTr: The overcrowding rate at correctional facilities nationwide has reached 126%, exacerbating problems including deteriorating working conditions for correctional staff, and increases in inmates with mental illness and drug-related offenses. Urgent measures for improvement are needed due to concerns over human rights violations and diminished rehabilitative effectiveness.

editorial.body: 정부가 비거주 1주택자의 종부세 기준을 9억 원으로 낮추고 양도세 장기보유공제를 축소하는 세제 개편을 단행했습니다. 전문가들은 이번 조치가 실거주자의 부담을 가중하고 공급 대책 없는 징벌적 과세가 되어 조세 형평성 논란과 시장 부작용을 일으킬 수 있다고 지적합니다.

editorial.titleTr: Opinion: Government vows not to control housing prices with taxes, yet penalizes single-homeowners
summaryTr: The government lowered the property tax threshold for non-resident single-home owners to 900 million won.
The burden on actual residents will increase due to the reduction in the long-term holding tax deduction for capital gains.
Experts express concerns about market side effects, calling it punitive taxation without supply measures.
editorial.bodyTr: The government has implemented tax reforms that lower the comprehensive real estate tax threshold for non-resident single-home owners to 900 million won and reduce the long-term holding deduction for capital gains tax. Experts point out that this measure could increase the burden on actual residents and become punitive taxation without supply measures, potentially raising concerns about tax equity and causing market side effects.

editorials.titleTr: Opinion: President Lee's Overseas Trips Total 26 Days Over Two Months
summaryTr: President Lee Jae-myung spent 26 days on overseas trips over a two-month period.
The presidential office emphasized achievements in economic cooperation.
Critics point out a repeat of past practices, including opposition party criticism amid domestic crisis.
editorials.bodyTr: Controversy has erupted over President Lee Jae-myung spending 26 days abroad over two months, including an 11-day tour of the United States and South America—the longest since taking office. While the presidential office emphasized achievements in economic cooperation, critics continue to point out that the president is repeating practices he had previously criticized during his time in the opposition, even as the country faces a domestic economic crisis marked by a sharp stock market plunge.

editorials.titleTr: Editorial: Presidential Approval Drops, Yet Gap Between Ruling and Opposition Parties Widens
summaryTr: Lee Jae-myung's presidential approval rating plummets below 50% as negative assessments surge
People Power Party also declines, widening gap with Democratic Party
Conservative camp reaches peak fatigue amid lack of leadership
editorials.bodyTr: President Lee Jae-myung's approval rating is declining as negative assessments surpass the 50 percent mark, while the People Power Party is also experiencing a corresponding drop, widening the support gap with the Democratic Party. As the ruling party fails to be recognized as a legitimate alternative force due to the absence of internal leadership and frequent conflicts, political fatigue among conservative and moderate voters has reached its peak.

leanScore.label: Center

[방송화면 캡처] 지난달 29일 오전 9시20분쯤 경기도 수원역 인근 거리에서 괴성을 지르며 제자리뛰기를 하고 길바닥에 엎드려 네 발로 기어다니는 등 이상 행동을 했던 여성이 마약투약 혐의로 경찰에 입건됐다. 수원팔달경찰서에 따르면 이 여성은 마약 간이검사에서 필로폰 양성반응이 나왔고, 필로폰 투약 혐의를 인정했다. 평일 출근시간에 수원역 거리를 ‘좀비’처럼 네발로 기어다닌 수원역 마약녀 사건은 단순히 개인의 일탈로 넘길 문제가 아니다. 어느덧 마약이 독버섯처럼 한국 사회 곳곳에 깊숙이 침투해 국민의 삶과 건강을 파괴하고 있는 장면을 상징한다고 봐야 한다. 문제의 심각성은 최근 유사한 사건들이 잇따르고 있다는 데 있다. 2월에는 30대 여성이 의료용 마약류인 프로포폴에 취한 상태로 스포츠카를 운전하다가 서울 반포대교 난간을 넘어 한강공원으로 추락한 사건도 있었다. 중국산 펜타닐에 찌든 미국과 과연 뭐가 다른가. 2021년 이후 국내 마약류 사범은 급증 추세다. 2023년에 처음 2만 명을 돌파하더니 그 후 3년 연속 2만 명 선을 웃돌고 있다. 경찰청 국가수사본부에 따르면 지난 3~6월 마약 사범 집중단속에서 5203명을 검거해 1039명을 구속했다. 검거된 마약사범 10명 중 약 4명은 SNS 등 온라인 비대면 거래로 마약을 유통하거나 구매한 것으로 드러났다. 이제 마약은 주부와 청소년 등 남녀노소를 가리지 않는다. 한국은 오랜 기간 ‘마약 청정국’이었다. 1989년 대검찰청에 전담수사조직인 마약과를 설치하고 체계적으로 마약 사범을 수사, 단속해 왔다. 하지만 2020년 문재인 정부가 검경 수사권 조정을 이유로 검찰의 마약수사 전담 조직을 축소하고, 검찰의 직접수사 개시 범위를 일부 마약 공급 범죄로 한정하면서 마약 수사가 크게 위축됐다. 경찰청은 3일부터 12월까지 마약 집중단속을 시작했다. 하지만 민주당의 검찰 보완수사권 전면 폐지로 오는 10월부터는 마약수사마저 검찰이 손을 떼게 된다. 경찰의 역량만으로 국제공조 등이 필요한 마약 수사를 제대로 할지 의구심이 드는 게 사실이다. 마약중독자와 마약 범죄는 느는데 수사 역량은 도리어 위축되는 상황이니 대한민국이 마약의 온상이 될까 우려하지 않을 수 없다.

editorial.titleTr: Editorial: A Nation Where Drug-Intoxicated Women in Their 20s Crawl Through Streets on All Fours
summaryTr: A woman in her 20s intoxicated by methamphetamine was found crawling on all fours at Suwon Station.
Drug offenses have surged since 2021, exceeding 20,000 cases annually.
Prosecutorial drug investigation capabilities are weakening due to reduced prosecutorial investigative authority.
editorial.bodyTr: Input Update Comprehensive Page 26. The Suwon Paldal Police Station announced that a woman who engaged in bizarre behavior such as jumping in place or crawling on all fours near Suwon Station in Gyeonggi Province during rush hour on the 29th of last month was booked on drug charges. [Broadcast screen capture] Around 9:20 a.m. on the 29th of last month, a woman who shouted strange noises while jumping in place and engaged in abnormal behavior such as lying face-down and crawling on all fours on the street near Suwon Station in Gyeonggi Province was booked by police on suspicion of drug use. According to the Suwon Paldal Police Station, the woman tested positive for methamphetamine in a simple drug test and admitted to methamphetamine use. The case of the Suwon Station drug-using woman who crawled on all fours "like a zombie" through Suwon Station streets during weekday rush hour cannot be dismissed as a mere individual deviation. It should be seen as symbolic of how drugs have quietly penetrated deep into various corners of Korean society like poisonous mushrooms, destroying citizens' lives and health. The severity of the problem lies in the succession of similar incidents occurring recently. In February, a woman in her 30s, intoxicated by propofol, a medical anesthetic, drove a sports car off the guardrail of Seoul's Banpo Bridge into the Han River Park. How different is this from America, tainted by Chinese-made fentanyl? Drug offenses nationwide have surged since 2021. For the first time in 2023, the figure surpassed 20,000, and for three consecutive years thereafter, it has remained above the 20,000 mark. According to the National Investigation Service of the National Police Agency, approximately 5,203 drug offenders were arrested during concentrated enforcement operations from March to June, with 1,039 of them detained. Approximately four out of every ten arrested drug offenders were found to have distributed or purchased drugs through online non-face-to-face transactions via social media and other platforms. Drugs now spare neither gender nor age, affecting housewives and teenagers alike. South Korea was long a "drug-free nation." In 1989, the Supreme Prosecutor's Office established the Drug Investigation Division as a dedicated investigation organization and systematically investigated and cracked down on drug offenses. However, in 2020, the Moon Jae-in government cited the adjustment of investigative authority between prosecutors and police as grounds to downsize the prosecution's dedicated drug investigation organization and limited the scope of direct prosecution investigations to some drug supply crimes, resulting in a significant contraction of drug investigations. The National Police Agency began concentrated enforcement operations against drugs starting the 3rd through December. However, with the Democratic Party's complete abolition of the prosecution's supplementary investigation authority, prosecutors will cease involvement in drug investigations starting October. There is legitimate doubt as to whether police capability alone can properly handle drug investigations that require international cooperation. With drug addiction and drug crimes increasing while investigative capacity actually contracts, concerns that South Korea could become a haven for drugs are unavoidable.

editorial.title: Justice weakened
editorial.body: Abolition of supplementary investigative powers risks weaker criminal investigations On July 31, the Democratic Party of Korea pushed through the National Assembly plenary session an amendment to the Criminal Procedure Act that abolishes not only prosecutors' authority to conduct direct investigations, but also their authority to carry out supplementary investigations. Cheong Wa Dae said it respects the National Assembly's legislative process and final decision, indicating that the president will not exercise his veto power. As a result, the abolition of prosecutors' authority to conduct supplementary investigations has all but been finalized. From Oct. 2, when the current Korean Prosecution Service is replaced by the Prosecutors’ Office and the Office of Serious Crimes Investigation, prosecutors will no longer be allowed to conduct supplementary investigations themselves, even if they find deficiencies in cases referred by the police. Despite the bill's sweeping overhaul of the nation's criminal investigation system and its far-reaching impact on public protection from crime, the Democratic Party pushed it through without sufficient deliberation or debate. The concerns of victims of crime and overwhelming public opposition were ignored, while only the party's political goal of completely stripping prosecutors of their investigative powers was achieved. This can only be seen as legislative overreach, using the parliamentary majority to push through legislation against the will of the people. The legislative process was so one-sided that it raised doubts about whether democracy was functioning properly in South Korea. Moreover, the party's last-minute insertion, without meaningful debate, of a clause expanding the grounds on which judges can dismiss prosecution raises doubts about the true intent in revising the law. The revised law adds two new grounds on which a judge may dismiss an indictment: when an investigation involved "serious illegality" or when prosecutors made a "gross abuse of prosecutorial discretion." Vague terms such as "serious" and "gross" give courts broad latitude to terminate trials arbitrarily. Expanding the grounds for dismissal of prosecutions, although existing precedents already allow courts to do so, raises suspicions that the real aim is to ensure that President Lee Jae Myung's criminal trials are terminated through a judge's dismissal of the prosecution when they resume after he leaves office — even if prosecutors do not withdraw the indictments. A Gallup Korea survey last month showed that public support for retaining supplementary investigative authority stood at 61 percent, far exceeding the 23 percent who favored its complete abolition. A majority of the public supports keeping supplementary investigative powers because they understand the harmful consequences of abolishing them. The truth that the “Gwangju high school girl murder case” was a sexually motivated killing, not a simple murder as police had treated it, emerged only after prosecutors’ further investigation. In the Busan spinning kick attack case, prosecutors also uncovered overlooked sex crime evidence through additional investigation, resulting in a harsher sentence for the perpetrator. The victim in the case made a public appeal to preserve supplementary investigative powers. There were widespread calls to retain the power to conduct supplementary investigations at least in cases involving vulnerable victims, such as women and people with disabilities, but they were rejected. The revised act leaves prosecutors with only the authority to request additional investigations. Even if prosecutors find new evidence of wrongdoing or identify shortcomings in a police probe, they must merely refer the matter back to the police for further investigation. In such cases, victims may have to give repeated statements, while cases risk being delayed as they are shuttled back and forth between the police and the prosecution office. If police inadequately respond to requests for supplementary investigations, it will only delay the resolution of cases. Ultimately, it is the public who will suffer the consequences. The Democratic Party must take full responsibility for hastily overhauling the nation’s criminal justice system without proper consideration. Although it appears highly unlikely that President Lee will veto the bill, he will also be unable to avoid responsibility if he chooses not to. 보충수사권 폐지, 약화된 수사로 이어질 우려

지난 7월 31일 민주당이 국회 본회의에서 검사의 직접수사권뿐 아니라 보충수사권까지 폐지하는 형사소송법 개정안을 통과시켰다. 청와대는 국회의 입법 절차와 최종 결정을 존중한다며 대통령의 거부권 행사 의사가 없음을 밝혔다. 결국 검사의 보충수사권 폐지는 사실상 확정되었다. 10월 2일 현재의 검찰이 검사청과 심각범죄수사청으로 분리되면, 검사들은 경찰로부터 송치된 사건에서 결함을 발견하더라도 더 이상 보충수사를 직접 수행할 수 없게 된다.

국가 형사수사 체계를 전면적으로 개편하고 국민의 범죄 피해 보호에 광범위한 영향을 미치는 법안임에도 불구하고, 민주당은 충분한 심의와 토론 없이 이를 강행했다. 범죄 피해자들의 우려와 압도적인 국민의 반대 의견을 외면하고 검사의 수사권을 완전히 박탈하려는 당의 정치적 목표만 달성했다. 이는 입법부의 과권이라 할 수 밖에 없으며, 국회의 다수당 지위를 이용해 국민의 의사에 반하는 법안을 강행한 것이다. 입법 과정이 너무도 일방적이어서 한국의 민주주의가 제대로 작동하고 있는지에 대한 의문을 제기하지 않을 수 없었다.

더욱 문제적인 것은 민주당이 마지막 순간에 충분한 토론 없이 판사의 공소기각 사유를 확대하는 조항을 몰래 삽입한 것이다. 개정안은 판사가 공소를 기각할 수 있는 새로운 사유로 수사 과정에서 '심각한 위법성'이 있었거나 검사가 '기소 재량권을 심각하게 남용'한 경우를 추가했다. '심각한'과 '심각하게'라는 모호한 표현은 법원에 광범위한 재량권을 부여하여 자의적으로 재판을 종료할 수 있도록 만든다. 기존 판례에서 이미 가능한 공소 기각 사유를 확대한 것은, 이준석 전 대표의 형사 재판이 재개되었을 때 검사가 공소를 제기하지 않더라도 판사의 기각으로 재판을 종료시키려는 의도 아닌가 하는 의심을 낳는다.

지난달 갤럽 여론조사에 따르면 보충수사권 유지에 대한 국민의 지지율은 61%로, 완전 폐지를 찬성하는 23%를 압도적으로 상회했다. 국민 다수가 보충수사권 유지를 지지하는 이유는 그것의 폐지가 초래할 해로운 결과를 잘 알고 있기 때문이다. '광주 여고생 살인 사건'의 진실이 단순 살인이 아닌 성범죄 살인임이 밝혀진 것은 검사의 추가 수사를 통해서였다. 부산 돌려차기 폭행 사건에서도 검사는 추가 수사를 통해 간과된 성범죄 증거를 적발해 가해자에게 더 무거운 형량을 받게 했다. 해당 사건의 피해자도 보충수사권 보존을 호소했다. 여성이나 장애인 등 취약 피해자 사건에 한해서라도 보충수사권을 유지해야 한다는 광범위한 주장이 있었으나 모두 거부되었다.

개정안에 따르면 검사에게는 추가 수사를 요청할 수 있는 권한만 남는다. 검사가 새로운 범죄 증거를 발견하거나 경찰 수사의 미흡함을 적발하더라도, 단지 해당 사건을 경찰에 회송하여 추가 수사를 요청할 수밖에 없다. 이 과정에서 피해자들은 반복적인 진술을 해야 하고, 사건은 경찰과 검사 사이를 오가며 지연될 위험에 노출된다. 경찰이 추가 수사 요청에 미흡하게 대응한다면, 사건 해결만 더 지연될 뿐이다. 결국 피해는 국민이 입게 될 것이다.

민주당은 충분한 검토 없이 국가 형사사법 체계를 성급하게 개편한 책임을 온전히 져야 한다. 비록 이준석 전 대표가 거부권을 행사할 가능성은 희박해 보이지만, 거부권 행사를 선택하지 않는다면 책임에서 자유로울 수 없을 것이다.

editorials.title: Justice weakened
editorials.body: Abolition of supplementary investigative powers risks weaker criminal investigations On July 31, the Democratic Party of Korea pushed through the National Assembly plenary session an amendment to the Criminal Procedure Act that abolishes not only prosecutors' authority to conduct direct investigations, but also their authority to carry out supplementary investigations. Cheong Wa Dae said it respects the National Assembly's legislative process and final decision, indicating that the president will not exercise his veto power. As a result, the abolition of prosecutors' authority to conduct supplementary investigations has all but been finalized. From Oct. 2, when the current Korean Prosecution Service is replaced by the Prosecutors’ Office and the Office of Serious Crimes Investigation, prosecutors will no longer be allowed to conduct supplementary investigations themselves, even if they find deficiencies in cases referred by the police. Despite the bill's sweeping overhaul of the nation's criminal investigation system and its far-reaching impact on public protection from crime, the Democratic Party pushed it through without sufficient deliberation or debate. The concerns of victims of crime and overwhelming public opposition were ignored, while only the party's political goal of completely stripping prosecutors of their investigative powers was achieved. This can only be seen as legislative overreach, using the parliamentary majority to push through legislation against the will of the people. The legislative process was so one-sided that it raised doubts about whether democracy was functioning properly in South Korea. Moreover, the party's last-minute insertion, without meaningful debate, of a clause expanding the grounds on which judges can dismiss prosecution raises doubts about the true intent in revising the law. The revised law adds two new grounds on which a judge may dismiss an indictment: when an investigation involved "serious illegality" or when prosecutors made a "gross abuse of prosecutorial discretion." Vague terms such as "serious" and "gross" give courts broad latitude to terminate trials arbitrarily. Expanding the grounds for dismissal of prosecutions, although existing precedents already allow courts to do so, raises suspicions that the real aim is to ensure that President Lee Jae Myung's criminal trials are terminated through a judge's dismissal of the prosecution when they resume after he leaves office — even if prosecutors do not withdraw the indictments. A Gallup Korea survey last month showed that public support for retaining supplementary investigative authority stood at 61 percent, far exceeding the 23 percent who favored its complete abolition. A majority of the public supports keeping supplementary investigative powers because they understand the harmful consequences of abolishing them. The truth that the “Gwangju high school girl murder case” was a sexually motivated killing, not a simple murder as police had treated it, emerged only after prosecutors’ further investigation. In the Busan spinning kick attack case, prosecutors also uncovered overlooked sex crime evidence through additional investigation, resulting in a harsher sentence for the perpetrator. The victim in the case made a public appeal to preserve supplementary investigative powers. There were widespread calls to retain the power to conduct supplementary investigations at least in cases involving vulnerable victims, such as women and people with disabilities, but they were rejected. The revised act leaves prosecutors with only the authority to request additional investigations. Even if prosecutors find new evidence of wrongdoing or identify shortcomings in a police probe, they must merely refer the matter back to the police for further investigation. In such cases, victims may have to give repeated statements, while cases risk being delayed as they are shuttled back and forth between the police and the prosecution office. If police inadequately respond to requests for supplementary investigations, it will only delay the resolution of cases. Ultimately, it is the public who will suffer the consequences. The Democratic Party must take full responsibility for hastily overhauling the nation’s criminal justice system without proper consideration. Although it appears highly unlikely that President Lee will veto the bill, he will also be unable to avoid responsibility if he chooses not to. editorial.titleTr: [Editorial] U.S. Drone Incident Should Prompt Seoul-Washington to Review Communication Channels
summaryTr: South Korean and U.S. militaries identified the cause of the unmanned aircraft misidentification incident as 'lax work procedures.'
The two countries failed to precisely follow the authorization procedures for special-use airspace flights.
An inspection of the communication system and improvement of procedures are urgently needed.
editorial.bodyTr: The core cause of the incident last month on the 30th, when our military nearly fired down a U.S. unmanned drone after mistaking it for an "unidentified flying object," has been identified as lax work practices by both South Korea and the United States in not precisely following the "special-use airspace flight authorization procedures." The U.S. military should have obtained flight authorization five days in advance.
